_meta.description: Family Courts formatting rules — established under the Family Courts Act, 1984. Exclusive jurisdiction over matrimonial, guardianship and maintenance matters
_meta.change_protocol: CLO sign-off required for any change. Vishal raises Jira tickets to Ajay for additions; never edits unilaterally.

jurisdictionNote: Family Courts established under Section 3 of the Family Courts Act, 1984. Exclusive jurisdiction over matrimonial relief (divorce, judicial separation, restitution, nullity, RCR), maintenance under Section 125 CrPC / Section 144 BNSS, guardianship and custody under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, and validity/legitimacy proceedings. Procedure under the Family Courts Act + applicable personal law (HMA 1955, SMA 1954, Divorce Act 1869, Muslim Personal Law, Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act 1936). Pleadings should be drafted to encourage settlement and conciliation.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, the Petitioner herein above named, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs ____ to ____ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ____ to ____ are true to my information and belief, and nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

PETITIONER
localRules: Procedure governed by the Family Courts Act, 1984 and Family Courts Rules framed by the respective High Court for the State.
Section 9 of the Act: duty of the Family Court to make efforts for settlement / reconciliation before adjudication; conciliation proceedings are mandatory.
Section 13 of the Act: parties not entitled to be represented by a legal practitioner as of right — leave of the court required (state practice varies).
Affidavit verifying the petition mandatory; non-judicial stamp paper requirement as per State.

In matrimonial petitions, territorial jurisdiction is fixed by the applicable personal law statute (e.g. Section 19 HMA 1955, Section 31 SMA 1954): place where the marriage was solemnised, where the respondent resides, or where the parties last resided together. The petitioner's own residence founds jurisdiction only where that statute allows it (e.g. a wife-petitioner under Section 19(iiia) HMA, or a respondent residing outside India or not heard of for seven years under Section 19(iv) HMA).

State the religion / personal law applicable to the parties where the relief depends on it (Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Parsi, Special Marriage Act). Do not state caste in the cause title or memo of parties.
Appeals from Family Court lie to the jurisdictional High Court under Section 19 of the Act within 30 days; orders for maintenance under Section 125 CrPC / 144 BNSS are revisable.

Tone of pleadings must remain dignified — avoid scandalous, frivolous, vexatious or unnecessarily inflammatory allegations; the Court may strike out such matter under Order VI Rule 16 CPC (applicable through Section 10(1) of the Family Courts Act, 1984).
